warrant.statement: The exact native noun linear-unit sense defines length, depth, or a standardized quantity of distance. Standardized units are orthogonal to anatomical structure. The reviewed source scope identifies ten exceptions where the defining magnitude explicitly depends on a body part. The horse application of the four-inch hand and historical stride origin of the standardized yard do not provide anatomical standards for those units. A native definition with a constitutive anatomical standard must receive an exact reviewed exception before this rule can apply.
